# typelua-leveldb

> A from-scratch LevelDB implementation in pure TypeLua (no C bindings). Byte-compatible on-disk format: WAL, MANIFEST, SSTables with bloom filters and CRC32C.

- [README](https://github.com/types-lua/typelua-leveldb#readme): API, options, quick start, limitations
- [DESIGN](https://github.com/types-lua/typelua-leveldb/blob/main/docs/DESIGN.md): module map, formats, recovery state machine, compaction rules
- [TypeLua docs](https://types-lua.github.io/docs/): language reference, FFI, concurrency, patterns
- [TypeLua SPEC](https://github.com/types-lua/TypeLua/blob/main/SPEC.md): language contract
- [Tests](https://github.com/types-lua/typelua-leveldb/blob/main/run_tests.tl): 1160 assertions across encoding, tables, engine and failure injection

## Use it

```lua
import leveldb from "leveldb"

local opened = leveldb.open("./data")
if opened.err ~= nil then error(opened.err.message) end
local db = opened.db

db:put("key", "value")
print(db:get("key").value)

local batch = leveldb.WriteBatch.new()
batch:put("a", "1")
batch:delete("key")
db:write(batch)

local it = db:newIterator()
it:seekToFirst()
while it:valid() do
  print(it:key(), it:value())
  it:next()
end
db:close()
```

## Run the suite

```bash
tlua check
tlua run run_tests.tl                  # embedded interpreter
tlua build && lua5.4 dist/run_tests.lua
tlua build --target 5.1 && luajit dist/run_tests.lua
```

## Facts an agent should not guess

- Fallible calls return **records**: `{ db, err }`, `{ found, value }`, `Error | nil`.
  There is no `(value, err)` tuple across module boundaries.
- Class methods are called with `:`; iterators expose `seek/seekToFirst/next/valid/key/value`.
- `db:close()` does **not** flush the memtable: the WAL is the durable copy and the next
  `open` replays it (this is the crash-recovery path, tested).
- Compaction is synchronous (`db:compactAll()` or automatic L0 pressure).
- Compression is not implemented; blocks are always type 0 (none).
- One writer per directory: there is no `LOCK` file.
